title: A bounded degree Borel graph on a Ramsey space has an independent tail

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Borel graph on a Ramsey space
standard_prerequisites.statement: A graph on the infinite subsets of the natural numbers with Borel edge relation and bounded degree.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the graph the statement is about.

standard_prerequisites.name: Tail-independent set
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set of the form [t,A] on which no two elements are joined by an edge.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vertex colouring of a bounded degree Borel graph
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every irreflexive bounded degree Borel graph admits a finite Borel vertex colouring, by the classical theorem of Kechris, Solecki and Todorcevic.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the cited theorem applied inside the proof.

core_obligations: Define an auxiliary graph on the interval [t,A] by declaring two elements adjacent when some restrictions of them are adjacent in the original graph (source lines 544-547).
Bound the degree of the auxiliary graph by two to the n times the degree of the original graph (source line 549).
Apply the colouring theorem to the auxiliary graph and take a colour class, which gives the required tail-independent set (source line 549).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the auxiliary graph by restricting the cut-off sequence.
Bound its degree and take a colour class.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 540-542: for a bounded degree Borel graph on the Ramsey space and a pair of finite and infinite data satisfying the standard ordering condition, there is an infinite subset of the given tail on which the induced graph has no edges. The proof (source lines 543-550) is short but does two things the statement does not show: it defines an auxiliary graph on the interval by declaring two elements adjacent when some of their restrictions are adjacent in the original graph, and it checks that this auxiliary graph is irreflexive with degree bounded by two to the n times the original degree; only then does the classical colouring theorem apply and a colour class give the independent tail. The statement records only the existence of the independent set.
